description: My name is Wade Rawlings. I spent thirty-one years in wildlife removal, starting in 1995 and learning how animals get into homes, where they hide, and why they keep coming back. From raccoons in attics and squirrels in walls to bats, snakes, mice, and birds finding their way through tiny openings, I learned one thing: the animal is rarely the real problem. The real problem is understanding how it got there, what attracted it, and what homeowners missed before it became a bigger problem.
